properties.text: All blob bytes submitted by an external blob submitter MUST be validated to have length exactly BYTES_PER_BLOB before any cryptographic processing occurs. Failure to enforce this allows buffer over-reads or under-reads in cell_to_coset_evals (SG-001), producing corrupted field elements that propagate through all downstream polynomial operations.

reachability.notes: Blob data originates from untrusted external submitters via P2P gossip or transaction submission. An attacker controls the blob content entirely.

properties.severity_justification: Bypassing blob length validation corrupts the entire polynomial commitment pipeline, potentially allowing forged data availability proofs that undermine consensus.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC should demonstrate submission of a malformed blob that bypasses length check and corrupts downstream cell computation.

properties.text: bytes_to_bls_field MUST reject any byte sequence representing a value >= BLS_MODULUS. If a field element deserialization accepts out-of-range values, polynomial arithmetic over BLS12-381 produces algebraically incorrect results, breaking KZG proof soundness.

reachability.notes: Attacker crafts blob bytes where a 32-byte segment encodes a value >= BLS_MODULUS. The bytes are directly controlled by the submitter.

properties.severity_justification: Out-of-range field elements break the algebraic guarantees of KZG commitments. A forged proof could pass verification for arbitrary data, defeating data availability.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires PoC demonstrating a blob with a field element >= BLS_MODULUS that is accepted and leads to incorrect polynomial evaluations.

properties.text: cell_to_coset_evals (SG-001) MUST produce exactly FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_CELL field elements from exactly FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_CELL * BYTES_PER_FIELD_ELEMENT input bytes. The byte-to-field-element mapping must be bijective: coset_evals_to_cell(cell_to_coset_evals(cell)) == cell for all valid cells.

reachability.notes: Cells originate from blob data which is attacker-controlled. Round-trip correctness is critical for data integrity.

properties.severity_justification: Non-bijective serialization means data loss or corruption in the encoding/decoding round-trip, breaking data availability guarantees.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC should show a cell value that encodes differently after round-trip through cell_to_coset_evals and coset_evals_to_cell.

properties.text: coset_evals_to_cell (SG-002) output MUST have exactly FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_CELL * BYTES_PER_FIELD_ELEMENT bytes. The output cell is the inverse of cell_to_coset_evals for valid field elements (SG-002/INV-002).

reachability.notes: coset_evals_to_cell is called during cell computation from attacker-provided blobs and during recovery from attacker-provided partial cells.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect cell serialization produces malformed sidecars that either crash peers or are silently accepted with wrong data.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Demonstrate a field element value that serializes to incorrect byte length.

properties.text: _fft_field (SG-003) input MUST have length that is a power of 2 and len(vals) MUST equal len(roots_of_unity). Violation causes incorrect recursive splits leading to wrong polynomial evaluations or infinite recursion.

validation_layers: Protocol constant enforcement (FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB is power of 2)
reachability.notes: While protocol constants are powers of 2, an implementation bug that allows non-standard lengths to reach FFT would be exploitable via crafted blobs.

properties.severity_justification: Non-power-of-2 input to FFT causes incorrect polynomial evaluation or stack overflow via infinite recursion, crashing the node.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Implementation-level PoC showing a code path where FFT receives non-power-of-2 length input.

properties.text: fft_field (SG-004) inverse FFT MUST apply normalization factor 1/N and reverse roots_of_unity order (except first element). Failure produces incorrect polynomial coefficient representations that propagate through KZG proof generation.

reachability.notes: FFT is invoked during blob-to-cell processing for every blob submission. Incorrect normalization would produce universally wrong proofs.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect inverse FFT normalization produces wrong polynomial coefficients for every blob, causing all KZG proofs to be invalid or, worse, causing acceptance of forged proofs.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC demonstrating that a specific blob produces proofs that fail verification due to normalization error.

properties.text: coset_fft_field (SG-005) MUST use PRIMITIVE_ROOT_OF_UNITY as shift_factor and the coset evaluation domain MUST avoid all points where vanishing polynomials evaluate to zero. This prevents division-by-zero during recovery (SG-023).

reachability.notes: An attacker who triggers recovery with specific missing cell patterns could potentially find evaluation points where the vanishing polynomial approaches zero on the coset, causing numerical instability.

properties.severity_justification: Division by zero during recovery crashes the node. Even near-zero divisors could produce numerically unstable results leading to incorrect recovery.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC showing a specific missing cell pattern that causes division by zero or numerically unstable recovery.

properties.text: compute_verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch_challenge (SG-006) MUST include ALL verifier-relevant data in the Fiat-Shamir hash input: domain separator, protocol parameters, all commitments, all commitment_indices, all cell_indices, all coset evaluations, and all proofs. Omitting any input allows an adversary to manipulate the challenge r.

reachability.notes: An attacker submitting cells/proofs for batch verification controls all inputs to the Fiat-Shamir hash. If any input is omitted from the hash, the attacker can craft inputs that produce a favorable challenge r.

properties.severity_justification: Incomplete Fiat-Shamir input allows forging batch verification proofs. An attacker could submit invalid data that passes verification, breaking data availability.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC demonstrating that omitting a specific field from the hash input allows crafting invalid proofs that pass batch verification.

properties.text: The Fiat-Shamir hash input order in SG-006 MUST be deterministic and canonical (SG-006/INV-003). Different orderings of the same logical inputs MUST NOT produce the same challenge. The domain separator RANDOM_CHALLENGE_KZG_CELL_BATCH_DOMAIN MUST be globally unique (SG-006/INV-002).

reachability.notes: Cross-protocol replay: an attacker could reuse a valid Fiat-Shamir challenge from another protocol context if domain separators collide.

properties.severity_justification: Domain separator collision enables cross-protocol proof replay. Non-canonical ordering enables proof substitution attacks within the same protocol.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC showing either a domain separator collision with another Ethereum protocol or a proof substitution via input reordering.

properties.text: polynomial_eval_to_coeff (SG-007) MUST apply bit_reversal_permutation BEFORE inverse FFT. The input polynomial MUST have exactly FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB evaluations. Incorrect permutation ordering produces coefficients for a different polynomial.

reachability.notes: Every blob submission triggers polynomial_eval_to_coeff. Incorrect bit-reversal produces a different polynomial whose degree may exceed trusted setup bounds.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect coefficient representation means proofs are generated for the wrong polynomial. If the resulting degree exceeds the trusted setup size, commitments become unsound.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC demonstrating that an implementation applies bit-reversal at the wrong stage, producing a polynomial that differs from the specification.

properties.text: multiply_polynomialcoeff (SG-009) MUST assert len(a) + len(b) <= FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_EXT_BLOB. The result degree MUST equal deg(a) + deg(b). Exceeding the degree bound means the polynomial cannot be committed with the trusted setup.

reachability.notes: Polynomial multiplication is used in interpolation (SG-011), vanishing polynomial construction (SG-012), and batch verification (SG-015). Attacker-controlled cell data determines polynomial degrees.

properties.severity_justification: Exceeding the trusted setup degree bound means g1_lincomb accesses out-of-bounds setup elements, causing a crash or producing an invalid commitment.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC showing polynomial degree overflow via crafted cell data during batch verification or recovery.

properties.text: divide_polynomialcoeff (SG-010) MUST NOT receive the zero polynomial as divisor (INV-001) and the leading coefficient of the divisor MUST be nonzero (INV-003). Division by zero in finite field arithmetic causes a runtime crash.

reachability.notes: divide_polynomialcoeff is called in compute_kzg_proof_multi_impl (SG-014) where the divisor is the vanishing polynomial. Crafted evaluation points could theoretically produce a zero vanishing polynomial.

properties.severity_justification: Division by zero crashes the node during proof generation. If triggered via P2P blob submission, this is a remote DoS.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC causing division by zero via a crafted set of evaluation points that produce a degenerate vanishing polynomial.

properties.text: interpolate_polynomialcoeff (SG-011) MUST receive all-distinct x-values (INV-001). Duplicate x-values cause division by zero in weight_adjustment = (xs[i] - xs[j]).inverse(). The result polynomial MUST have degree at most len(xs) - 1 and evaluate correctly at all interpolation points.

reachability.notes: interpolate_polynomialcoeff is called inside verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch_impl (SG-015) with coset elements as x-values. If cell_indices map to overlapping coset points, duplicate x-values could occur.

properties.severity_justification: Division by zero during batch verification crashes the verifier node. Attacker can submit crafted cell_indices targeting duplicate coset points.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC with crafted cell_indices that cause duplicate x-values in interpolation during batch verification.

properties.text: vanishing_polynomialcoeff (SG-012) output MUST evaluate to 0 at every point in xs, have degree exactly len(xs), and be monic (leading coefficient = 1). Incorrect vanishing polynomial construction breaks KZG proof generation quotient computation.

reachability.notes: Vanishing polynomial is computed from coset points derived from cell_indices, which are attacker-controlled in batch verification.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect vanishing polynomial produces wrong quotient in KZG proof generation, causing valid blobs to produce invalid proofs or invalid blobs to produce valid proofs.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC showing a vanishing polynomial that does not vanish at all specified points.

properties.text: compute_kzg_proof_multi_impl (SG-014) quotient polynomial Q(X) MUST satisfy f(X) = Q(X) * Z(X) + I(X) where I(X) is the interpolation polynomial of f at the evaluation points zs. The proof commitment MUST use KZG_SETUP_G1_MONOMIAL with deg(Q) within the trusted setup bounds.

reachability.notes: Proof generation is triggered for every blob. The polynomial comes from attacker-controlled blob data.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect quotient polynomial produces proofs that either fail verification (DoS for honest blobs) or pass verification for invalid data (consensus failure).
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC demonstrating a blob that produces an incorrect quotient polynomial due to an implementation bug.

properties.text: verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch_impl (SG-015) verification equation e(LL, LR) == e(RL, [1]) MUST hold if and only if all (commitment, cell, proof) tuples are valid. The random challenge r MUST bind all inputs via the Fiat-Shamir heuristic. The pairing check MUST reject with overwhelming probability for any invalid tuple.

reachability.notes: Batch verification is the primary cryptographic gatekeeper for data availability. All inputs (commitments, cells, proofs, cell_indices) are attacker-controlled when submitted via P2P.

properties.severity_justification: Bypassing batch verification allows an attacker to convince the network that unavailable data is available, breaking the fundamental data availability guarantee and potentially enabling invalid state transitions.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC demonstrating invalid cells/proofs that pass batch verification.

properties.text: verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch_impl (SG-015) MUST validate that all input lists have equal length, commitments list contains no duplicates (INV-003), and all commitment_indices reference valid entries in the commitments list (INV-004). Missing validation allows out-of-bounds access or incorrect weight accumulation.

reachability.notes: All inputs to batch verification are attacker-controlled. Missing bounds checks on commitment_indices could cause out-of-bounds array access.

properties.severity_justification: Out-of-bounds commitment_index causes a crash (DoS). Duplicate commitments with incorrect deduplication could cause weight accumulation errors leading to false verification results.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC with out-of-bounds commitment_indices or duplicate commitments causing incorrect verification.

properties.text: verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch (SG-021) public API MUST validate: all input lists have equal length (INV-002), each commitment has exactly BYTES_PER_COMMITMENT bytes, each cell_index < CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB (INV-004), each cell has exactly BYTES_PER_CELL bytes, and each proof has exactly BYTES_PER_PROOF bytes. Failure to validate any of these allows malformed inputs to reach the pairing check.

reachability.notes: This is the outermost public verification API. All inputs are directly attacker-controlled bytes from P2P messages.

properties.severity_justification: Missing input validation at the public API boundary allows malformed data to reach cryptographic operations, potentially causing crashes, memory corruption, or verification bypass.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC with malformed byte lengths that bypass validation and cause unexpected behavior in the pairing check.

properties.text: Proof reuse across different (commitment, cell) pairs MUST be detected and rejected by batch verification. The Fiat-Shamir challenge computation (SG-006) includes commitment_indices, cell_indices, coset evaluations, and proofs, ensuring that any substitution changes the challenge r and invalidates the verification equation.

reachability.notes: An attacker copies a valid proof from one (commitment, cell) pair and presents it for a different pair. The Fiat-Shamir challenge must change to reject this.

properties.severity_justification: Successful proof reuse breaks binding of proofs to commitments, allowing data availability forgery.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC demonstrating proof substitution between different commitment/cell pairs that passes batch verification.

properties.text: coset_shift_for_cell (SG-016) MUST assert cell_index < CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB. The returned coset shift h is the generator of the coset h*G where G is the subgroup of order FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_CELL. An out-of-bounds cell_index causes out-of-bounds array access in roots_brp.

reachability.notes: cell_index is attacker-controlled in batch verification (SG-015) and recovery (SG-024). Missing bounds check allows out-of-bounds memory access.

properties.severity_justification: Out-of-bounds cell_index causes array index out of bounds, crashing the node (remote DoS via P2P).
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC with cell_index >= CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB that reaches coset_shift_for_cell and causes a crash.

properties.text: coset_for_cell (SG-017) MUST return exactly FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_CELL elements from the bit-reversal-permuted roots of unity. The elements MUST form the coset h*G = {h, h*g, h*g^2, ...} where h = coset_shift_for_cell(cell_index). Incorrect coset computation breaks both proof generation and verification.

reachability.notes: coset_for_cell is called during cell computation (SG-018), proof generation (SG-019), and batch verification (SG-015). All paths are reachable via blob submission or proof verification.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect coset elements mean polynomial evaluations are computed at wrong points, producing cells that fail verification or, worse, allowing data substitution.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC demonstrating coset computation mismatch between proof generation and verification paths.

properties.text: compute_cells (SG-018) MUST produce exactly CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB cells, where each cell represents polynomial evaluations over a distinct coset of the extended domain. The blob MUST be exactly BYTES_PER_BLOB bytes (INV-001). Each cell MUST be verifiable against the blob's KZG commitment.

reachability.notes: compute_cells is called for every blob received via P2P. The blob content is fully attacker-controlled.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect cell count or evaluation points produce sidecars that either fail peer validation (DoS) or contain incorrect data (data integrity violation).
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC showing a blob that produces an incorrect number of cells or cells evaluated at wrong coset points.

properties.text: compute_cells_and_kzg_proofs_polynomialcoeff (SG-019) MUST produce CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB cells and proofs where each proof is valid for its corresponding cell and coset. The O(n^2) complexity (INV-003) means adversarial blobs can cause significant computational cost.

reachability.notes: Every blob triggers CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB proof generations, each involving polynomial division and g1_lincomb. O(n^2) total cost per blob.

properties.severity_justification: Resource exhaustion via computationally expensive proof generation. The O(n^2) complexity is inherent to the algorithm; mitigation requires rate limiting or FK20 optimization.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC demonstrating meaningful resource exhaustion by submitting blobs that maximize proof generation time.

properties.text: compute_cells_and_kzg_proofs (SG-020) public API MUST validate blob length == BYTES_PER_BLOB and delegate correctly to compute_cells_and_kzg_proofs_polynomialcoeff after conversion through blob_to_polynomial and polynomial_eval_to_coeff.

reachability.notes: Public API entry point for blob processing. Blob content is fully attacker-controlled.

properties.severity_justification: Missing blob length validation at the public API allows undersized or oversized blobs to reach polynomial processing, causing buffer errors or incorrect cell generation.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC with non-standard blob size bypassing the public API validation.

properties.text: recover_polynomialcoeff (SG-023) MUST satisfy E(x) * Z(x) == P(x) * Z(x) over the FFT domain (INV-001). Division by Z(x) MUST be performed over a coset domain to avoid division by zero (INV-002). The recovered polynomial MUST have degree < FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB (INV-003).

reachability.notes: An attacker provides partial cells for recovery via P2P. The cells could be individually valid but mutually inconsistent (from different polynomials), causing recovery of a wrong polynomial.

properties.severity_justification: Recovering the wrong polynomial from adversarial cells produces incorrect cells and proofs that could be re-distributed, poisoning data availability across the network.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC providing inconsistent cells from different blobs that cause recovery of a polynomial different from the original.

properties.text: recover_polynomialcoeff (SG-023) MUST verify that high-degree coefficients of the recovered polynomial (indices FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB through FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_EXT_BLOB - 1) are zero. Non-zero high-degree coefficients indicate adversarial or inconsistent input cells. Truncation to FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB coefficients (INV-003) discards this check.

reachability.notes: If truncation silently discards non-zero high-degree coefficients without verification, the recovered polynomial differs from the original. The spec recommends post-recovery verification against the KZG commitment.

properties.severity_justification: Silent truncation of a higher-degree recovered polynomial means the regenerated cells/proofs are for a different polynomial. Without post-recovery commitment verification, this goes undetected.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC providing cells that recover to a polynomial with non-zero high-degree coefficients, demonstrating data corruption after truncation.

properties.text: recover_cells_and_kzg_proofs (SG-024) MUST validate: len(cell_indices) == len(cells) (INV-001), at least CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB / 2 cells provided (INV-002), cell_indices are unique and sorted (INV-003), all cell_indices < CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB (INV-004), and all cells have correct byte length.

reachability.notes: Recovery is triggered when a node receives partial cells via P2P during data availability sampling. All inputs are from untrusted peers.

properties.severity_justification: Missing validation allows duplicate cell_indices (leading to wrong recovery), out-of-bounds indices (memory corruption/crash), or insufficient cells (incorrect polynomial recovery).
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC with duplicate cell_indices, out-of-bounds indices, or fewer than 50% cells that bypasses validation.

properties.text: recover_cells_and_kzg_proofs (SG-024) MUST require at least CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB / 2 cells (50% threshold) for recovery. Below this threshold, Reed-Solomon erasure coding cannot uniquely determine the original polynomial.

reachability.notes: An attacker withholding cells can force a node to attempt recovery with insufficient cells. If the 50% threshold is not enforced, the node would produce an incorrect polynomial.

properties.severity_justification: Recovery below the 50% threshold produces an arbitrary polynomial. If no post-recovery verification exists, the incorrect data propagates through the network.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC showing recovery with fewer than 50% cells that produces an incorrect polynomial without error.

properties.text: The KZG trusted setup (KZG_SETUP_G1_MONOMIAL, KZG_SETUP_G2_MONOMIAL) MUST be honestly generated with all toxic waste destroyed. G1 and G2 setup elements MUST be from the same ceremony and validated against known checksums. Compromised setup enables forging proofs for arbitrary polynomials.

reachability.notes: Trusted setup integrity is a ceremony-level assumption. Runtime compromise requires supply-chain attack on setup file distribution.

properties.severity_justification: Compromised trusted setup breaks the entire KZG commitment scheme. All proofs become forgeable.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Trusted setup integrity is outside the scope of implementation-level bug bounties. However, supply-chain attacks on setup file distribution may be in scope.

properties.text: KZG_SETUP_G2_MONOMIAL[n] used in the pairing check (SG-015 q_lr) MUST correspond to the same trusted setup as KZG_SETUP_G1_MONOMIAL. A mismatch between G1 and G2 setup elements could cause the verification equation to accept invalid proofs or reject valid ones.

reachability.notes: G1/G2 mismatch requires supply-chain attack or incorrect configuration.

properties.severity_justification: G1/G2 mismatch silently breaks all verification. Valid proofs may be rejected (consensus failure) or invalid proofs accepted (data availability forgery).
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Configuration-level issue, not typically in bug bounty scope unless the loading code has a bug.

properties.text: The hash function used in hash_to_bls_field MUST behave as a random oracle for the Fiat-Shamir heuristic to be sound (asm-003). A weak or predictable hash function allows an adversary to pre-compute the challenge r and craft inputs that pass batch verification for invalid proofs.

reachability.notes: If the hash function has exploitable weaknesses (e.g., length extension, collision-finding shortcuts), an attacker can manipulate the Fiat-Shamir challenge.

properties.severity_justification: Weak hash function in Fiat-Shamir breaks the non-interactive proof system entirely.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC demonstrating a hash function weakness that allows challenge prediction or collision.

properties.text: bit_reversal_permutation MUST be applied consistently across all code paths: polynomial_eval_to_coeff (SG-007), coset_shift_for_cell (SG-016), coset_for_cell (SG-017), and recover_polynomialcoeff (SG-023). Any inconsistency produces misaligned evaluations between encoding and decoding.

reachability.notes: Inconsistent bit-reversal between encoding (blob -> cells) and decoding/verification paths means cells produced by honest validators fail verification.

properties.severity_justification: Inconsistent permutation between proof generation and verification means all honestly-generated proofs fail verification, causing a consensus split.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC demonstrating that encoding and verification use different permutation orderings for the same cell_index.

properties.text: compute_roots_of_unity MUST produce primitive roots of unity of the correct order for the BLS12-381 scalar field. PRIMITIVE_ROOT_OF_UNITY (SG-005/INV-001) MUST be a genuine primitive root. Incorrect roots make FFT and coset evaluations algebraically meaningless.

reachability.notes: PRIMITIVE_ROOT_OF_UNITY is a compile-time or configuration constant. Incorrect value would break all polynomial operations for all blobs.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect primitive root breaks all FFT operations, making the entire polynomial commitment system non-functional.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Static constant validation; not typically in scope unless a build system bug produces an incorrect constant.

properties.text: get_validators_custody_requirement (SG-001, validator spec) MUST return a value in [VALIDATOR_CUSTODY_REQUIREMENT, NUMBER_OF_CUSTODY_GROUPS]. The custody requirement MUST be proportional to total_node_balance via BALANCE_PER_ADDITIONAL_CUSTODY_GROUP. The clamping MUST enforce both minimum and maximum bounds.

reachability.notes: If the beacon state is forked or stale, effective_balance values used for custody computation could be incorrect. An attacker with sufficient stake influence could manipulate custody assignments via state manipulation.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect custody requirements could create coverage gaps for certain columns, reducing data availability below the recovery threshold for specific blobs.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC showing custody requirement bypass via stale state that creates a coverage gap for data availability.

properties.text: cells_and_kzg_proofs_construction (validator SG-002) MUST correctly align cells and proofs: blobs_bundle.proofs MUST have length CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB * len(blobs_bundle.blobs) (INV-002), and proof slicing indices [start:end] MUST always be in bounds (INV-003). Misaligned proof slicing produces invalid sidecars.

reachability.notes: blobs_bundle comes from the execution layer via Engine API. A malicious or buggy execution client could provide misaligned proofs.

properties.severity_justification: Misaligned cell-proof pairs produce sidecars that fail verification at all receiving peers, preventing data availability for that block.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC with blobs_bundle having incorrect proof count or ordering that produces invalid sidecars.

properties.text: get_data_column_sidecars (validator SG-003) MUST produce exactly NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS sidecars. Each sidecar MUST contain exactly one cell and one proof per blob (INV-003). DataColumnSidecar.index MUST equal the column_index used to select the cells (INV-004).

reachability.notes: Incorrect sidecar construction causes peers to reject valid block data or accept data from wrong columns.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect sidecar.index assignment means data is published to the wrong subnet, preventing peers from finding the data they need for availability sampling.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC showing sidecar construction with incorrect column_index assignment.

properties.text: get_data_column_sidecars_from_block (validator SG-004) Merkle inclusion proof MUST target the blob_kzg_commitments field at its correct generalized index in the BeaconBlockBody SSZ tree. Incorrect proof depth or leaf index causes all sidecars to be rejected by peers.

reachability.notes: The Merkle proof computation depends on the SSZ container structure for the Fulu fork. Fork-specific changes to BeaconBlockBody could change the generalized index.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect Merkle proof causes all sidecars for the block to fail inclusion proof verification, effectively making the block's blob data unavailable.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC showing incorrect generalized index for blob_kzg_commitments in the Fulu fork BeaconBlockBody.

properties.text: Each data column sidecar MUST be published to exactly one subnet determined by compute_subnet_for_data_column_sidecar(column_index) (validator SG-006/INV-001). The subnet mapping MUST be deterministic and consistent across all nodes (INV-002). Publishing to the wrong subnet prevents peers from receiving data.

reachability.notes: An inconsistent subnet mapping between different implementations causes data columns to be published where no one expects them, breaking data availability.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect subnet routing for data column sidecars breaks data availability sampling for all peers expecting data on a specific subnet.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC showing implementation disagreement on subnet assignment for a specific column_index.

properties.text: Validators MUST retain sidecars for at least MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_DATA_COLUMN_SIDECARS_REQUESTS epochs (validator SG-007/INV-001) and MUST serve them on request during this period (INV-002). Premature pruning degrades data availability.

reachability.notes: An attacker can flood a validator with requests during the retention period (DoS via tb-012). The MUST serve requirement creates an amplification vector.

properties.severity_justification: Premature pruning by a single validator only degrades data availability marginally. However, systematic premature pruning across multiple validators could prevent recovery.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC demonstrating a request flood that causes a validator to violate its retention/serving obligations.

properties.text: An adversary MUST NOT be able to infer a validator's custody group membership by probing which columns the validator serves (tb-012/InfoDisclosure). Response timing MUST NOT differ based on whether a column is in the validator's custody set.

reachability.notes: An attacker probes a validator by requesting different columns and measuring response times to infer custody group membership.

properties.severity_justification: Custody group membership leakage reveals validator identity and position in the shuffling algorithm, enabling targeted attacks.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC demonstrating custody group inference via response time analysis.

properties.text: A validator MUST NOT claim to have published sidecars while actually withholding them (data withholding attack, tb-010/Repudiation). Data availability sampling by multiple independent peers MUST detect withheld data with high probability.

reachability.notes: A malicious validator with sufficient stake could withhold data columns, degrading data availability below the recovery threshold.

properties.severity_justification: Successful data withholding by a coalition of validators prevents recovery, blocking finality for blocks with blob transactions.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC demonstrating a data withholding strategy that evades detection by data availability sampling.

properties.text: A network-level adversary MUST NOT be able to selectively drop or delay data column sidecars to prevent data availability below the 50% recovery threshold (tb-010/DoS). The custody group system MUST provide sufficient redundancy.

reachability.notes: An adversary controlling network infrastructure could selectively drop specific subnet traffic to degrade data availability.

properties.severity_justification: Network-level censorship of specific columns prevents recovery if enough columns are dropped below the 50% threshold.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC demonstrating subnet-level censorship that prevents data recovery for a specific blob.

properties.text: Custody requirement computation (validator SG-001) MUST use the finalized or justified beacon state to prevent fork-based manipulation. A stale or forked state could produce incorrect custody assignments that create coverage gaps.

reachability.notes: An attacker who can cause a validator to use a forked state could manipulate custody requirements. Requires an active fork attack.

properties.severity_justification: Fork-based custody manipulation requires significant validator power and only affects validators that follow the wrong fork.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC showing custody requirement change due to state fork that creates a coverage gap.

properties.text: Low-staked validators coordinating to collectively reduce data availability coverage for specific columns MUST be mitigated by VALIDATOR_CUSTODY_REQUIREMENT (minimum floor of 8) ensuring every validator stores at least a baseline number of columns (tb-011/EoP).

reachability.notes: An attacker could create many minimum-stake validators to minimize their individual custody burden, creating collective coverage gaps.

properties.severity_justification: Requires significant capital (many minimum-stake validators) and coordination. The minimum floor of 8 groups limits the attack surface.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC showing a validator set composition that creates a column with insufficient custody coverage.

properties.text: Batch verification (SG-015) computational cost scales linearly with num_cells, including polynomial interpolations (SG-011), g1_lincomb operations, and a pairing check. An adversary MUST NOT be able to submit arbitrarily large batches to cause unbounded resource consumption (tb-007/DoS).

reachability.notes: An attacker submits a large batch of (commitments, cells, proofs) causing expensive verification operations. Maximum batch sizes should be bounded by protocol constants.

properties.severity_justification: Resource exhaustion via large batch verification. The single pairing check optimization limits the attack surface, but interpolation and g1_lincomb costs scale linearly.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC demonstrating meaningful resource exhaustion via oversized batch verification requests.

properties.text: Recovery (SG-023) computational cost includes multiple FFTs, inverse FFTs, coset FFTs, and element-wise operations over vectors of size FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_EXT_BLOB. An adversary providing the minimum 50% of cells maximizes vanishing polynomial size and thus computational cost (tb-008/DoS).

reachability.notes: An attacker withholds cells strategically to force recovery with minimum cells (maximum vanishing polynomial degree), maximizing computational cost.

properties.severity_justification: Recovery is inherently expensive. Triggering repeated recovery for non-canonical blocks wastes node resources.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC showing repeated recovery triggering with minimum cells causing meaningful resource exhaustion.

properties.text: construct_vanishing_polynomial (SG-022) MUST produce a polynomial that evaluates to zero at all missing cell evaluation points (INV-002). At least one cell MUST be present (INV-001). The coefficient spacing by FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_CELL (INV-003) MUST correctly extend the polynomial to the full domain.

reachability.notes: Missing cells are determined by which cells the attacker chooses not to provide. Incorrect vanishing polynomial construction breaks recovery entirely.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect vanishing polynomial causes recovery to produce the wrong polynomial, leading to incorrect cells and proofs being redistributed.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC showing a specific missing cell pattern that causes incorrect vanishing polynomial construction.

properties.text: BLS12-381 cryptographic hardness (asm-002) MUST hold for all KZG commitments, proofs, and pairing-based verification to be secure. Specifically, the discrete logarithm problem in G1/G2 and the bilinear Diffie-Hellman assumption in the pairing group MUST be computationally hard.

reachability.notes: Fundamental cryptographic assumption. A break in BLS12-381 security would affect all systems using this curve, not just this protocol.

properties.severity_justification: A break in BLS12-381 discrete log or pairing assumptions would allow forging arbitrary KZG proofs, completely defeating data availability.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Cryptographic assumption; outside implementation-level bug bounty scope.

properties.text: The pairing check e(LL, LR) == e(RL, [1]) in verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch_impl (SG-015/INV-001) MUST be sound: it rejects with overwhelming probability when the underlying KZG polynomial commitment relationship does not hold. The universal verification equation MUST aggregate multiple cell proofs into a single pairing check (INV-005).

reachability.notes: An implementation error in the pairing check (e.g., wrong point negation, incorrect lincomb) could cause false acceptances.

properties.severity_justification: Unsound pairing check allows forged proofs to pass verification, completely breaking data availability guarantees.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC demonstrating an implementation bug in the pairing check that causes false acceptance of invalid proofs.

properties.text: get_data_column_sidecars_from_column_sidecar (validator SG-005) MUST validate len(cells_and_kzg_proofs) == len(sidecar.kzg_commitments) and correctly reuse header, commitments, and inclusion proof from the existing sidecar. Failure to validate causes delegation to get_data_column_sidecars with mismatched inputs.

reachability.notes: Sidecars received from peers are untrusted. Reconstructing sidecars from received data without validation could produce invalid output.

properties.severity_justification: Missing validation causes incorrect sidecar reconstruction, potentially producing sidecars with mismatched cells and commitments.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC with mismatched cells_and_kzg_proofs and kzg_commitments lengths bypassing assertion.
